bottleneck: When embryos or zygotes are edited, the editor often acts after cell division has begun, producing mosaic organisms where only some cells carry the edit. Mosaicism makes outcomes unpredictable: a therapy may appear to work while unedited cells continue driving disease, or a germline edit may transmit unevenly to offspring. Single-cell analysis reveals mosaic patterns that bulk sequencing misses entirely. In human embryo research this undermines both safety assessment and any therapeutic claim, since no measurement can confirm uniform editing.
current_state: Faster-acting editors and earlier delivery reduce but do not eliminate mosaicism. It remains a central scientific objection to any clinical embryo-editing proposal.

sources.title: A double-edged sword: CRISPR-Cas9 is emerging as a revolutionary technique for genome editing

title: Mosaicism undermines embryo genome editing
why_it_blocks: Mosaicism turns a precise edit into a genetic lottery within one organism, with different tissues carrying different genomes. No regulator can approve embryo editing while a substantial fraction of cells may escape or misinterpret the edit.
